priorStories.headline: Australian lawmaker loses leg after vehicle attack
priorStories.body:
Australian independent lawmaker Helen Haines was in critical condition after surgery and the amputation of one leg following a deliberate vehicle attack in Wangaratta.

Officials said the vehicle struck Haines, reversed and hit her again before a bystander restrained the driver. Counterterrorism authorities were helping investigate, but police had not established a motive or filed charges.

priorStories.headline: Japan launches mission to sample Mars moon
priorStories.body:
Japan launched its uncrewed Martian Moons eXploration spacecraft aboard an H3 rocket from Tanegashima Space Center.

The mission is designed to study Mars’s moons, collect at least 10 grams of material from Phobos and return it to Earth in 2031. If successful, it would be the first sample return from the Martian system.

priorStories.headline: Kenyan cult members convicted of 191 murders
priorStories.body:
A Kenyan court convicted preacher Paul Mackenzie and 28 associates of murdering 190 children and one adult in the Shakahola Forest.

The court found that Mackenzie’s followers were ordered to starve themselves and their children, while guards prevented victims from escaping or eating. More than 400 bodies have been recovered during the wider investigation. Sentencing was set for November 6.

priorStories.headline: WFP drops 500,000 people from Gaza aid
priorStories.body:
The U.N. World Food Programme said funding shortages were forcing it to reduce planned monthly food or cash assistance in Gaza from 1.6 million people to 1.1 million.

The reduction leaves about 500,000 people without monthly assistance while roughly two-thirds of Gaza’s population remains acutely food insecure, according to the agency.

priorStories.headline: Houthi attack kills 58 at Yemen camp
priorStories.body:
Three ballistic missiles struck a government security-forces training camp in Yemen’s Shabwa province, killing 58 people and injuring more than 200, according to the provincial governor. Fourteen people remained missing.

The Houthis acknowledged targeting the Al-Alam camp, which they described as Saudi-run.

candidates.summary: CBC News projected that Alberta voters rejected starting the legal process toward a binding referendum on separation from Canada after about one-third of ballots had been counted. The province’s first separation referendum was nonbinding and offered voters a choice between remaining in Canada and initiating that process.
candidates.title: Alberta voters reject separation process in referendum

candidates.summary: A Russian drone struck morning traffic near a shopping center in Chabany on the Kyiv–Odesa highway, setting vehicles on fire and killing three people, according to Ukrainian prosecutors. Four others were wounded, and emergency crews restricted traffic while authorities investigated and verified the preliminary casualty count.
candidates.title: Russian drone strike kills three on Kyiv–Odesa highway

candidates.summary: Unofficial results from Elections Alberta showed voters decisively rejecting the option to begin the legal process toward a binding referendum on separation from Canada. With more than 1.8 million votes counted and 81% of voting locations reporting, about 75% supported remaining in Canada and 25% supported beginning the separation process.
candidates.title: Alberta voters decisively reject separation process

candidates.summary: A senior Yemeni government official said the death toll from the previous day's Houthi ballistic-missile strike on the Al-Alam military training camp had risen from 58 to 73. The official said all those killed were new recruits and more than 200 people were injured.
candidates.title: Death toll from Houthi strike on Yemen camp rises to 73

candidates.summary: The United Kingdom announced additional defensive military support for Saudi Arabia amid escalating Houthi attacks. RAF Typhoon fighters will fly defensive counter-air missions over Saudi territory, while an A400M transport aircraft and British military advisers will also be deployed. The UK government said the Typhoons would not conduct offensive strikes against the Houthis.
candidates.title: UK expands defensive military support for Saudi Arabia

candidates.summary: Abyei's caretaker information minister said the confirmed death toll from Monday's drone strike on Amiet Market had risen from 73 to 153 as fires and recovery efforts continued. He blamed Sudan's military but provided no evidence, and Sudan's military had not responded. The strike hit a fuel-selling area in the territory disputed by Sudan and South Sudan.
candidates.title: Toll from Abyei market drone strike rises to 153

candidates.summary: NATO said it would send additional maritime patrol aircraft, radar systems, drones, intelligence personnel and forensic teams to the Black Sea following deadly attacks on merchant shipping. NATO did not attribute the recent attacks to a country. The announcement followed a North Atlantic Council discussion of regional security.
candidates.title: NATO adds surveillance assets in Black Sea

candidates.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv was again receiving allied early warnings about incoming Russian ballistic missiles after a call with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Zelenskyy had said the warnings were absent for at least a week. Rubio acknowledged frustrations over intelligence and weapons supplies but said U.S. policy had not changed and denied a deliberate directive to harm Ukraine.
candidates.title: Zelenskyy says allied missile warnings have resumed

candidates.summary: Local authorities said the death toll from Monday's drone strike on Amiet Market had risen to more than 220, up from the 153 reported earlier Tuesday. Recovery efforts were continuing after the strike ignited fuel stores. Abyei officials blamed Sudan's military, which had not publicly responded to the accusation.
candidates.title: Abyei market strike toll rises above 220

candidates.summary: Libya's eastern-based House of Representatives unanimously approved a disputed 2019 maritime-boundary agreement with Turkey. The chamber also repealed 2020 resolutions that had rejected the agreement and called for severing political relations with Ankara. Greece rejected the deal, saying it violated international law.
candidates.title: Eastern Libya parliament approves Turkey maritime deal

candidates.summary: Nigeria confirmed an imported case of Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus in Abuja. The patient was a woman who had recently arrived on a flight from Uganda and had received care at a private hospital before laboratory confirmation. Authorities activated public-health response measures, including isolation, contact tracing and monitoring of health workers.
candidates.title: Nigeria confirms imported Ebola case in Abuja

sources.name: Nigeria Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare
World Health Organization Regional Office for Africa

candidates.summary: Kenya's Health Ministry confirmed a ninth Ebola infection. Officials said the patient was a close contact of the country's first confirmed patient and had tested positive while in quarantine. Kenya's initial case involved a traveler who arrived from the Democratic Republic of the Congo via Uganda and later died in Nairobi.
candidates.title: Kenya's confirmed Ebola cases rise to nine

sources.name: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

candidates.summary: The European Commission and the EU's foreign-policy chief presented a new Arctic strategy emphasizing security, climate resilience and economic development. Proposed measures include increased satellite surveillance, monitoring of undersea cables, support for icebreaker purchases, a polar research hub and development of a Pan-Arctic communications cable linking Greenland with Europe.
candidates.title: European Union presents new Arctic strategy

candidates.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff, Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre and Finnish President Alexander Stubb in Oslo, with U.S. envoy Jared Kushner joining remotely. Norway said the talks covered Ukrainian security, postwar reconstruction and territorial issues and described the discussions as constructive. European and NATO security officials later joined a working dinner.
candidates.title: Ukraine and allies hold peace-framework talks in Oslo

sources.name: Norwegian Office of the Prime Minister
Office of the President of Ukraine

candidates.summary: Two dozen independent U.N. human-rights experts called for an investigation into Indian authorities' conduct during recent opposition and student protests. They cited reports of force against unarmed demonstrators, arbitrary detentions, assembly restrictions, surveillance and internet disruptions. India's Election Commission and governing party deny protesters' claims that revisions to voter lists unfairly removed eligible voters.
candidates.title: UN experts seek investigation of policing at India protests

candidates.summary: Israeli strikes and gunfire killed at least four Palestinians in separate incidents in Gaza, according to health officials. An airstrike killed a married couple in a Gaza City apartment, while medics reported that Israeli gunfire killed a 17-year-old near Khan Younis and another person in eastern Gaza City.
candidates.title: Israeli fire kills at least four Palestinians in Gaza
